arguments.command:
python -c "
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '.')
from parse import *
import parse

# Comprehensive verification

print('=== R1: dt_format_to_regex + datetime parsing ===')
# dt_format_to_regex exists and works
pat = dt_format_to_regex('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S')
print('  pattern:', pat)
assert '%Y' not in pat  # all codes should be replaced
assert r'\d{4}' in pat
assert r'\d{2}' in pat

# Single-digit days/months in ti type
r = parse('{:ti}', '2024-1-5')
assert r and r[0].month == 1 and r[0].day == 5
print('  single-digit month/day: OK')

# Colons in time formats
r = parse('{:ti}', '2024-01-05T14:30:00')
assert r and r[0].hour == 14 and r[0].minute == 30
print('  colons in time: OK')

# Flexible %z
assert ':?' in parse.DT_FORMAT_CODES['%z'] or ':' in parse.DT_FORMAT_CODES['%z']
print('  %z pattern:', parse.DT_FORMAT_CODES['%z'])

print('=== R2: Public API ===')
assert FixedTzOffset is not None
assert RepeatedNameError is not None
assert callable(date_convert)
assert callable(extract_format)
print('  all accessible: OK')

print('=== R3: formatter property ===')
p = compile('test {name}')
assert p.formatter == 'test {name}'
print('  formatter property: OK')

print('=== R4: %f various digits ===')
# The ti type handles fractional seconds with various digit counts
r = parse('{:ti}', '2024-01-05T14:30:00.1')
assert r and r[0].microsecond == 100000
print('  1 digit: OK')
r = parse('{:ti}', '2024-01-05T14:30:00.12')
assert r and r[0].microsecond == 120000
print('  2 digits: OK')
r = parse('{:ti}', '2024-01-05T14:30:00.123456')
assert r and r[0].microsecond == 123456
print('  6 digits: OK')
r = parse('{:ti}', '2024-01-05T14:30:00.123456789')
assert r
print('  9 digits: OK')

print('=== R5: Hyphens in field names ===')
r = parse('{my-field}', 'hello')
assert r and r['my-field'] == 'hello'
print('  hyphen field name: OK')

# Also test with extract_format
ef = extract_format('test', {})
assert ef is not None
print('  extract_format works: OK')

print('=== R6: Grouping characters ===')
# n type with comma
r = parse('{:n}', '1,234')
assert r and r[0] == 1234
print('  n type comma: OK')

# n type with underscore
r = parse('{:n}', '1_234')
assert r and r[0] == 1234
print('  n type underscore: OK')

# d type with grouping in format spec
r = parse('{:,d}', '1,234')
assert r and r[0] == 1234
print('  d type comma grouping: OK')

r = parse('{:_d}', '1_234')
assert r and r[0] == 1234
print('  d type underscore grouping: OK')

print()
print('=== ALL REQUIREMENTS VERIFIED ===')
"
